claims.statement: Tom Allen lost his title to Joe Goss on a foul, disqualified in the 21st round, on an island near Covington, Kentucky, on 7 September 1876.
claims.excerpt: Joe Goss on an island near Covington, Ky., on Sept. 7, 1876

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Bill Davis in 43 rounds on Chouteau Island in 1869.
claims.excerpt: finishing off Bill Davis in 43 rounds on Chouteau Island

claims.statement: In 1869 Tom Allen issued a challenge to Bill McCoole.
claims.excerpt: Chouteau Island and issued a challenge to McCoole

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Bill McCoole on Carpenter's Island on 15 June 1869; the bout was stopped and the referee later gave the decision to McCoole.
claims.excerpt: met on Carpenter’s Island on June 15, 1869

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Bill McCoole on Chouteau's Island on 23 September 1871, in a rematch.
claims.excerpt: a rematch on Sept. 23, 1871, on Chouteau’s Island. Allen beat McCoole into a bloody pulp in three or four rounds

claims.statement: Jem Mace beat Tom Allen by a knockout in the 10th round at Kennersville, Louisiana, about a year after the 1869 McCoole fight.
claims.excerpt: took on Allen at Kennersville, La., won on a 10th-round knockout

claims.statement: Allen's claim to the title stood without dispute until he lost on a foul to Joe Goss.
claims.excerpt: claim to the title was without dispute then until he lost on the foul to Joe Goss

claims.statement: Two years after losing the title, Tom Allen returned to his native England, and on 22 May 1878 ceremonies were held in London in his honour.
claims.excerpt: Two years later he returned to his native England and on May 22, 1878, appropriate ceremonies to honor him took place

claims.statement: On 22 May 1878 in London, Tom Allen was presented a silver cup inscribed as champion boxer of England by his friends and admirers.
claims.excerpt: Presented To Tom Allen, Champion Boxer of England, by his buddies and admirers
places: Cambridge Hall, Newman St. and Oxford St., London

claims.statement: Allen's silver cup was retrieved from a Market Street pawn shop in 1938 by the father of Thomas Allen Taylor.
claims.excerpt: My father retrieved this cup from a pawn shop

claims.statement: In 1978 Allen's silver cup was in the home of his great-grandson Thomas Allen Taylor.
claims.excerpt: That cup today holds a place of honor in the home

claims.statement: Allen's daughter Mary, called Polly, returned to the United States with him and later married Edward Taylor of St. Louis.
claims.excerpt: called Polly, returned to the United States with him and she subsequently

claims.statement: Polly Allen Taylor and Edward Taylor were the grandparents of Thomas Allen Taylor, Allen's great-grandson.
claims.excerpt: They are the grandparents of Thomas Allen Taylor

claims.statement: Allen's will left everything to his daughter Polly Allen Taylor and to a friend, Tillie Hartgrove.
claims.excerpt: Polly Allen Taylor, and to a friend, Tillie Hartgrove

claims.statement: When Allen's will was probated, his estate amounted to $278.35.
claims.excerpt: The will amounted to $278.35

claims.statement: Tom Allen died on 6 April 1903, still operating Sportsmen's Rest.
claims.excerpt: which he continued to operate until he died on April 6, 1903
places: Sportsmen's Rest, Market Street, St. Louis

claims.statement: Allen's saloon, Sportsmen's Rest, was on Market Street between 6th and 7th, St. Louis, where the old American Theater once stood.
claims.excerpt: Allen’s saloon was called Sportsmen’s Rest and was
places: Market Street between 6th and 7th, St. Louis

claims.statement: Arguments at Allen's saloon that could not be settled with words were settled with bare hands in the back room, against the law.
claims.excerpt: the principals retired to the back room, accompanied by anybody

claims.statement: Allen had the liquor concession at the island fights.
claims.excerpt: The whole thing was not a total loss for Allen. He had the liquor concession.

claims.statement: Allen's face was lined with scars, and he had a terrible scar on his right hand.
claims.excerpt: His face was lined with scars. He had another terrible scar on his right hand.

claims.statement: In later years Allen's hands were shapeless, with the knuckles gone from pounding.
claims.excerpt: Pictures of him in later years showed his hands to be shapeless hunks

claims.statement: In his fight with Charley Gallagher a shot was fired, the ball struck Allen's hand, a doctor removed it, and the fight went on.
claims.excerpt: In a fight with one Charley Gallagher, someone fired a shot

claims.statement: Allen lost interest in boxing and retired after the Marquis of Queensberry refined the rules.
